correctness.rationale: I solved the stages with a common x and checked the full row update symbolically (`python3 /workspace/checks/sdirk_birth.py`, SymPy 1.14). With U=(I−hxB)^−1 the two stage operators are U and (I+h(1−2x)UB)U. The completed update is I+h(U+stage2)B/2; every entry matches, row sums are one, and the two relevant discriminants and −1/16 coefficient agree. The transient block has shift distance at most three and only its diagonal r_0 and the four-jump absorbing corner a_4 can be negative. For 0<h<1/3 the numerator 3−4x+hx(4x−1) strictly decreases in x and crosses exactly once between 3/4 and 1; from h=1/3 on it is nonnegative everywhere since at h=1/3 the sign is that of (x−1)(4x−9). The diagonal is nonnegative for h≤2. For h>2 its numerator is negative at x=1/2 and its larger root determines the successful upper interval, which collapses at 1+sqrt(3) to the singleton x=1 and is empty above it. This singleton is correctly assigned probability zero, although the short open-interval phrasing about nonemptiness in Proof Step 4 should be read with its following endpoint clarification. Uniform interval lengths give both nonconstant branches; at h=0 the update is the identity. Row lumping or the same transient calculation for n≤4 eliminates a_4, giving minimality in the stated family. The h^4 corner expansion is uniform on the parameter interval and integrating its leading coefficient gives −1/16, so expectation cannot restore stochasticity for all sufficiently small positive h. I inspected but did not run the frozen checker; exact stage algebra plus sign analysis, not binning, establishes the continuous law.

value.rationale: Stochasticity of a numerical transition matrix is a natural preservation property not guaranteed by scalar norm stability. With just five absorbing-birth states, almost half the draws fail at arbitrarily small positive steps, the ensemble mean also fails, yet a finite interval recovers stochasticity for every draw. The minimal dimension and complete probability law make this a usable test of positivity claims for stiff solvers. The scope is one step, this generator family and this parameter law, not nonlinear positivity or arbitrary Markov matrices.
